paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The Teacher says a lot of our hustle springs from envy, and he calls it "futile and a pursuit of the wind" (Ecclesiastes 4:4). He also shows us the man with no end to his labor who asks, "For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?" (Ecclesiastes 4:8). Working yourself empty to stay ahead of somebody who never signed up for the race is a SAD way to spend your days.

So what's the better way? "Two are better than one," because they have "a good return for their labor" (Ecclesiastes 4:9). When one falls, the companion can lift him up, and "a cord of three strands is not quickly broken" (Ecclesiastes 4:10, 12). I know a little about falling down alone, and I promise the oven is NOT a helpful witness.

This matters for your week, baker. Your life is not meant to be a solo sprint where you collect more and enjoy less. Hold your one handful with peace (Ecclesiastes 4:6), and keep people close who will pick you up. Even the youth who went from prison to the crown will not be celebrated by those who come even later (Ecclesiastes 4:14, 16), so spend your days on what lasts: the people beside you.
